references.citation: Gan TJ, Belani KG, Bergese S, et al. Fourth Consensus Guidelines for the Management of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 2020;131(2):411-448.
references.excerpt: Scopolamine transdermal patch is effective for PONV prophylaxis, especially in patients with a history of motion sickness. It should be applied the evening before or at least 2 to 4 hours before surgery. The patch delivers 1.5 mg of scopolamine over 72 hours.

references.label: Eberhart 2004 POVOC
references.citation: Eberhart LH, Geldner G, Kranke P, et al. The development and validation of a risk score to predict the probability of postoperative vomiting in pediatric patients. Anesth Analg. 2004;99(6):1630-1637.
references.excerpt: Four independent risk factors for postoperative vomiting in children were identified: duration of surgery of at least 30 minutes, age 3 years or older, strabismus surgery, and a history of postoperative vomiting in the child or of postoperative vomiting/nausea in relatives. The incidence of postoperative vomiting was 9%, 10%, 30%, 55% and 70% for the presence of none, one, two, three and four of these risk factors.

references.label: BJA 1999 Paediatric PONV
references.citation: Rose JB, Watcha MF. Postoperative nausea and vomiting in paediatric patients. Br J Anaesth. 1999;83(1):104-117.
references.excerpt: Postoperative vomiting occurs about twice as frequently in children as in adults, and is one of the commonest causes of unanticipated hospital admission after ambulatory surgery. Risk increases with age up to adolescence, with duration of surgery, and with particular operations such as strabismus repair, adenotonsillectomy and orchidopexy; prophylaxis should be reserved for children at increased risk and combinations of drugs acting at different receptors are more effective than single agents.

references.label: BJA 2009 TAP Caesarean
references.citation: Belavy D, Cowlishaw PJ, Howes M, Phillips F. Ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane block for analgesia after caesarean delivery. Br J Anaesth. 2009;103(5):726-730.
references.excerpt: Transversus abdominis plane block after caesarean delivery reduced morphine requirements in the first 24 h and reduced nausea, supporting opioid-sparing regional techniques as part of a multimodal strategy in this high-risk group.

references.label: A&A 2022 PONV Rescue
references.citation: Weibel S, Schaefer MS, Raj D, et al. Drugs for preventing and treating postoperative nausea and vomiting in adults: an updated evidence synthesis. Anesth Analg. 2022;135(6):1226-1240.
references.excerpt: For established postoperative nausea and vomiting, treatment should use an antiemetic from a pharmacological class different from that used for prophylaxis, with the underlying trigger sought and treated; repeating the same drug within six hours confers little additional benefit while increasing adverse effects.

cards.question: What is the Apfel score and how does it guide PONV prophylaxis?
cards.answer: Four risk factors: female sex, non-smoker, history of PONV/motion sickness, postoperative opioid use. Each scores 1; predicted risk 10/20/40/60/80 %. Score 0–1: no prophylaxis or 1 agent. Score 2: 2 agents. Score 3–4: 3 agents + consider TIVA + avoid N₂O. Use drugs from different classes (5-HT3 antagonist + steroid + droperidol or cyclizine).

cards.question: Compare the mechanisms of common antiemetics.
cards.answer: Ondansetron — 5-HT3 antagonist at vagal afferents and chemoreceptor trigger zone; QT prolongation. Dexamethasone — anti-inflammatory and central effects; given at induction (delayed onset 1–2 h, duration 24 h). Cyclizine — H1 antihistamine + anticholinergic; useful for opioid- and motion-related PONV; tachycardia limits use in cardiac disease. Droperidol — D2 antagonist; effective but QT prolongation black-box. Aprepitant — NK1 antagonist; long-acting (24 h).

cards.question: What is the role of TIVA in PONV?
cards.answer: Propofol TIVA reduces PONV incidence by ~25 % compared with volatile anaesthesia (number needed to treat ~6 for high-risk patients). Mechanism is multifactorial — antiemetic action of propofol at low concentrations and avoidance of emetogenic volatiles. Combine with avoidance of N₂O, opioid-sparing techniques (regional, NSAIDs), and a multimodal antiemetic regimen for highest-risk patients.
